claim.claim-text: 1. A combination therapy comprising (a) a replicative oncolytic vaccinia virus engineered to express GM-CSF and (b) an antibody that selectively binds to PD-1 for use in the treatment of renal cell carcinoma in a human subject.
2. The combination for use according to claim 1, wherein the oncolytic vaccinia virus comprises a deactivated thymidine kinase gene.
3. The combination for use according to claim 1 or 2, wherein the replicative oncolytic vaccinia virus is administered intratumorally intravenously, intra-arterially, or intraperitoneally.
4. The combination for use according to any one of claims 1-3, wherein the replicative oncolytic vaccinia virus is a Wyeth Strain.
5. The combination for use according to any one of claims 1-4, wherein the vaccinia virus comprises functional 14L and/or F4L genes.
6. The combination for use according to any one of claims 1-5, wherein the antibody that selectively binds PD-1 is a monoclonal antibody.
7. The combination for use according to any one of claims 1-4, wherein the renal cell carcinoma is metastatic renal cell carcinoma.

8. The combination for use according to any one of claims 1-7, wherein the subject has failed at least one previous chemotherapy or immunotherapy, preferably wherein the subject has a cancer that is refractory to an immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy, preferably wherein the cancer is resistant to treatment with anti-PD-1 antibodies and/or anti-PD-L1 antibodies.

9. The combination for use according to any one of claims 1-8, wherein the replicative oncolytic vaccinia virus is administered multiple times at a dose of 1×10<8> to 1×10<9> plaque forming units (pfu), preferably at a dose of 1×10<9> pfu.
10. The combination for use according to any one of claims 1-9, wherein the replicative oncolytic vaccinia virus is administered weekly.
11. The combination for use according to any one of claims 1-10, wherein the antibody that selectively binds PD-1 is administered multiple times at a dose of 2 mg/kg to 15 mg/kg.
12. The combination for use according to any one of claims 1-11 wherein the antibody that selectively binds PD-1 is administered at least once every month.

13. The combination for use according to any one of claims 1-12, wherein the replicative oncolytic vaccinia virus and the antibody that selectively binds PD-1 are administered concurrently, wherein concurrent administration comprises administering said oncolytic vaccinia virus and said anti-PD-1 antibody within 12, 11, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 hours or within 1 hour of each other.

14. The combination for use according to any one of claims 1-13, wherein the combination therapy provides improved antitumoral effects relative to single administration of either the replicative oncolytic vaccinia virus or the antibody that selectively binds PD-1.
